newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Staff to get 10 pct of Senegal telecom shares.
newsitem.headline: Staff to get 10 pct of Senegal telecom shares.

text.p: Senegal will reserve 10 percent of shares in state telecommunications company SONATEL for employees under any privatisation, Communications Minister Serigne Diop said in a statement on Thursday.
"Ten percent of SONATEL's shares will be reserved to the staff of the company within the framework of the opening of the capital," Diop said, giving no further details.
France Telecom has started formal talks with the state privatisation committee on the purchase of a one-third stake in SONATEL.
Senegal's Telecoms trade union recently complained that it had been left in the dark about the authorities' plans.
France Telecom stepped in after the cancellation on April 16 by Senegal of a provisional deal worth 70 billion CFA francs ($120 million) with a consortium led by Swedish company Telia Overseas.
The consortium wanted a seven-year concession which would have lasted only until the proposed end of the company's monopoly over the fixed-line network.
Senegal plans to sell the remaining two-thirds of SONATEL to private Senegalese and other African investors.
